name: FormPublisher
title: start a FormWeb site from a template, check it, package it and host it yourself
summary: FormPublisher starts FormWeb sites from templates, checks, packages and signs them, and prepares a folder for your own host, on your computer with no account and no monthly subscription.
lede: FormPublisher is the do-it-yourself version of a site builder, with no monthly subscription. Start from a template, edit it in FormWeb, then check, package and sign it here, and host it yourself with the guide, paying only your own host and domain. It runs locally with no account, and it hosts nothing, uploads nothing and buys no domain.
runs_on: macOS 13 or newer on Apple silicon, macOS 14 or newer on Intel, Windows and Linux
checks: Starts a site from eight FormWeb templates, each file checked against its SHA-256, or imports a FormWeb export, a .fweb project, a publication folder or the site open in FormWeb, and never changes it.

Checks the files offline (links, assets, metadata, headings, forms, canonical links, Open Graph, hreflang, a favicon and a 404 page) and, in a deep check, layout shift, largest contentful paint and text contrast.
Builds a deterministic site.zip with a publish.json that lists every file by SHA-256, reproduces it byte for byte and signs it with an Ed25519 key kept in your system's password store.
Prepares a folder for Static zip, Netlify, Cloudflare Pages, Vercel, GitHub Pages or nginx with the exact commands to run, and uploads nothing.

facts.dd: .fpub holds a build's publish.json, site.zip and signature, and the same build always saves to the same bytes
A vanilla TypeScript and Vite interface, a Python and FastAPI engine and a Tauri 2 desktop shell
Static zip, Netlify, Cloudflare Pages, Vercel, GitHub Pages and nginx, with a hosting guide for each

chapters.title: What Wix and Squarespace set up for you, checked
chapters.text: Static checks run offline on the files: links, assets, redirects, sitemap, robots, metadata, images, headings, forms that post to a local address, canonical links, Open Graph tags, structured data, reciprocal hreflang, a favicon, a 404 page, link names and form labels. A deep check drives the Chrome or Edge you already have and measures layout shift, largest contentful paint and text contrast.

chapters.title: One package, the same bytes every time
chapters.text: Build a deterministic site.zip with a publish.json that lists every file by SHA-256, reproduce it byte for byte, and sign it with an Ed25519 key. The key's private half is kept in your system's password store, and Verify tells you whether a package was signed by one of your own keys.

chapters.title: A folder for your host, and the commands to run
chapters.text: Prepare a folder for Static zip, Netlify, Cloudflare Pages, Vercel, GitHub Pages or nginx, with the redirects, headers and 404 rule that host expects and the exact commands to run. You pay your host and your domain, nothing else, and nothing is ever uploaded.

features.title: Start from a template
features.text: The Templates sheet starts a site from eight FormWeb starters, read from a fixed release of formai-templates only when you press Get the templates.
bullets: Business, portfolio, blog, event and shop site types, with a filter
Every file and preview checked against its SHA-256
A FormWeb project written into a folder you choose

features.title: Reads FormWeb
features.text: Opens a site-export.zip, a .fweb project, a .fpub package, a publication folder, or the site open in a running FormWeb, and never changes it.
bullets: FormWeb's Send to FormPublisher, or its inbox folder when FormPublisher is closed
Read-only toward FormWeb
A site that arrives again gains a revision

features.title: Preview
features.text: The site is served by a static host on its own origin, as a real host would, with every route in a strip beside the stage.
bullets: Device sizes, dark or light, reduced motion
Network throttled to Fast or Slow
The current route opens in your browser

features.title: Checks
features.text: Static checks run offline on the files, live checks read the console, failed requests and layout shift from the preview, and a deep check measures speed and contrast.
bullets: Search and sharing: canonical links, Open Graph, structured data, hreflang
Accessibility: link names and form labels
Each rule names its source in the manual

features.title: Package and sign
features.text: A deterministic site.zip with a publish.json, reproduced byte for byte and signed with an Ed25519 key from your system's password store.
bullets: Inspect a build and compare two
Save a build as one .fpub file
Keys managed in Preferences, under Signing keys

features.title: Publish
features.text: A prepared folder for each of six hosts, written from the build's own site.zip, verifiable against publish.json, and never uploaded.
bullets: Static zip, Netlify, Cloudflare Pages, Vercel, GitHub Pages and nginx
FormWeb's model files left out unless you keep them
The last Verify result kept beside each folder

features.title: Host it yourself
features.text: The hosting guide takes the folder FormPublisher wrote to your host: the steps, your domain's DNS records, HTTPS, updates, forms and analytics.
bullets: A part for each of the six hosts
A live-site check after you deployed it, which reads only
No host recommended over another and no affiliate link

features.title: Agent tools
features.text: 28 command line commands and 30 MCP tools cover the whole path from a template or an import to a prepared folder and its verify, so Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and Antigravity do what a person does in the window.
bullets: An agent dock in the window with a tab for each agent found
Each tool says whether it reads, writes in the data folder or writes to a path you named
Deleting for good stays a person's action

features.title: Trash and revisions
features.text: Removed sites, builds, keys and prepared folders wait in a Trash on Home, and a site's revisions show the files and routes changed between any two.
bullets: Restore puts an entry back where it came from
Delete for good and Empty Trash ask first
Rebindable keyboard shortcuts

features.title: A window you know
features.text: Home, one tab per open site, a menubar, a routes strip, an inspector and a bottom panel, in the Form family's look with dark and light themes and a green accent.
bullets: 26 interface languages
Panels that resize by dragging or by keyboard
The manual inside the window, with the network off too

requirements: Rust 1.97.0 and the Tauri prerequisites, only for the desktop window
docs.install:
git clone git@github.com:nodemode-dev/formpublisher.git
cd formpublisher
./formpublisher_oc_install
./setup/install_compiler
Windows: formpublisher_oc_install.bat
docs.desktop: ./build_app builds the desktop app start to finish and logs to build_app.log; ./formpublisher desktop dev opens the desktop window over the source tree.
docs.agents: ./formpublisher mcp starts the MCP server on stdio, and ./formpublisher agents install registers it with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and Antigravity.

topics.title: Quick Start
topics.text: The interface is at http://localhost:5280 and the engine on 127.0.0.1:8280. ./formpublisher doctor checks the toolchain.

topics.title: Manual
topics.text: docs/MANUAL.md is the manual, also in the app under Help > Documentation.

topics.title: Host it yourself
topics.text: docs/HOSTING.md takes a prepared folder to Netlify, Cloudflare Pages, Vercel, GitHub Pages, nginx or any static host, with DNS, HTTPS, updates, forms and analytics.

topics.title: Configuration
topics.text: FORMPUBLISHER_HOME moves the data folder (~/FormPublisher by default), FORMPUBLISHER_PORT sets the engine port and FORMPUBLISHER_HOST_PORT the preview host port.

topics.title: Status
topics.text: In development. Importing from the site open in FormWeb needs FormWeb running on the same computer. Publish prepares folders but never uploads. The deep check needs Chrome and the optional requirements-deep.txt; .fweb projects need formweb-core.
